title: Detention and Mixtape
premise: Jonah Montrose has survived fifteen years in her rust-belt town by being flawless and invisible—debate trophies up, head down, especially around her father's drinking and the school board seat he lost under murky circumstances. When debate coach Ms. Okafor pairs her with Theo Vasquez, the expelled-and-reinstated troublemaker who knows what really happened at Harlan High a decade ago, their semester project on 'institutional memory' becomes an excavation of the asbestos cover-up that sickened students, including Theo's older brother. As Jonah's careful world cracks—her father's name is all over the buried minutes—she must choose between protecting her family's fragile peace and exposing the truth before the championship final, where she plans to use her rebuttal time to say what no one else will. She wins the round, loses the trophy to disqualification, and gains something better: a found family of truth-tellers and a father finally forced to face what his silence cost.
about_author: W. M. Kavanagh is a former high school debate coach who spent seven years watching teenagers say braver things in rounds than adults said in board meetings. They write from a small apartment above a laundromat, surrounded by old yearbooks and other people's secrets.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ms. Okafor announces semester partners: Jonah with Theo Vasquez, the boy whose brother got sick at Harlan and whose grudge against the school is legendary. Their first project meeting in the library archive is a disaster of clashing methods—his blunt digging versus her polished caution. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Jonah feels her invisibility strategy failing for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Minutes Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In sealed 2009 school board minutes, they find Jonah's father's signature approving a cheap asbestos abatement—and a list of affected students including Theo's brother Marcus. Theo accuses; Jonah defends her father out of reflex, then can't sleep. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden; Jonah realizes silence was the family heirloom, and she's next in line for it.

chapters.title: Rebuttal
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, climax. The regional final arrives as the school board moves to expel Theo for 'archive tampering.' Mid-round, instead of her prepared case, Jonah delivers the buried evidence as her constructive speech—naming the cover-up, her father, and herself. The gym goes silent; her father walks out; the judges disqualify her. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, and freedom on the other side of it.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, resolution. A local reporter picks up the story; the state opens an investigation; Marcus gets the apology letter he stopped waiting for. Theo makes Jonah a mixtape—track one is her own final speech, recorded off a phone in the gym. Her father shows up at the door, sober, asking to talk. Emotional beat: found family assembled from wreckage; survival redefined as living loudly.
